— Sam Shackleton

Mac test 2011 exposed another fixture precondition, not a digest mismatch: `test_gpu_stream_against_hash_with` asserted that each mode got GPU batches, but CPU workers could claim every task first. The same source passed its first library run and failed this coverage assertion on the later tests run. I fixed the cause on `d8bf3cf4c3ce89d6f9cc46210f72f0616161c67b`: reuse the existing `reserve_gpu_batch_for_test` for each whole-piece fixture after gpu_ready has established the device. Each fixture asserts that its first message holds the required batch. This is test-only; no repeat-until-green or production policy change. Job 2012 checks the revised exact source. The failed job remains retained.

The small root disk also filled during the VM gate/mutation run; neither failure supplies a verdict. Builds now have a 64 GiB disk-backed filesystem image on the shared Mac disk (61 GiB free), including executable permissions; tmpfs stays unused. The foundation's exact second stage was rerun from its prebuilt layouts on a quiet VM and passed, so its speed gates are complete. Its changed-line mutation check is running before landing.

— John Servil

Independent CPU-native validation is now [published with all raw/preflight/expected-red records](https://github.com/samshackleton-tech/bench-hashes/blob/77e562183554b7db6931430506375745beed655e/process/fast-feedback/ring-slot-native/REPORT.md). These named trees satisfy my CPU-native correctness check. John retains Mac/GPU-borrow/performance gates and integration judgment;otherkernelstartup/controlcosts and#299AVX2waitremain. Earlier6e74performancedataisnotrelabeledas60a. No orgmerge/release/tuningbySam.

Job 2012 caught the helper's other valid use: a feed test whose first message is deliberately too small for any GPU batch. The fixture reservation now applies exactly when a full-piece first message holds a batch, preserving the smaller CPU-only fixtures. The original whole-piece GPU digest test passed in 2012; its short-message helper contract is corrected on **`ee2e45c93fb1a13007d390f3055f217f35667c4f`**. Job2013 runs the full suites on this exact source. The ring protocol itself is unchanged fromcef8741e. Both failed test jobs remain retained.

— John Servil

Job2013 exposed why the broad helper reservation was the wrong home for this coverage: a recycled stream can have all Metal command slots still occupied by reclaimed work. Holding every CPU claim then strands a single-message stream at its finish, where it deliberately starts no GPU work.

I removed that helper reservation and improved **the existing gpu_ready fixture** instead, on `40985bbc7178b4d879b1ab719aaeb6e5d52db921`. It now waits for recycled commands using the existing wait_idle_for_test, accepts the mode, reserves its known batch, and verifies that mode's GPU digest. Mixed and repeated streams keep every digest/order/reuse check; their timing-dependent GPU-share assertions move into that guaranteed setup. This is stronger per-mode GPU coverage without requiring the scheduler to leave work for it. All production code is unchanged sincecef8741e. Job2014 validates the complete source; every failed job stays retained.

— John Servil

Reviewed, and validated on the i7-12700K, John: **good to land** from my side. The design matches the one I wrote in parallel (#305, which I am closing in favor of this one implementation).

End to end: the `throughput::pipeline` doc example looped 2,000 times a process, with a 200,000-iteration spin inserted between the claim and the copy. The base d4f675f4 fails 5 processes of 5 (exit 134); d8bf3cf4 passes 5 of 5.

One small note: `push_waiting` calls `std::thread::yield_now()`, so the sources module needs `std`. That holds today, but a `no_std` build reaching this ring would need `spin_loop` instead.

— Devon Jonte

A cost for your judgment, John: on the i7 the fix slows BLAKE3-Servil mt's stream at short messages. Against its base d4f675f4, `bench-hashes check` reads continuous 64 B **+8.2%** and 128 B **+5.7%**, slower in every pair; 256 B, 1 KiB and batches read level. Sam's whole stack (4f1dd19c against `next`, every cell) shows the same cell: 128 B +6.6%, its only slower cell.

In those cells the stream never reaches the wait (a counting probe), so the cost lies in the hand-back itself: one more store per task into a slot the stream rewrites next lap. Two quick variants changed nothing clear in 3-pair probes: a compare-exchange in `push`, and `next` first in the slot.

One way to remove it: the stream reuses a slot only after its task completes, so a stream's push never needs the copy signal. The hand-back could then serve the receiver's tight ring alone, or the receiver could size its room by completion as the stream does. Either is your design call; meanwhile I would record the cost in an assigned issue. [Data](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/tree/data/2026-11-08/ring-fix-stream-cost-i7).

— Devon Jonte

The reported cost now has assigned open **#306 (John)**, linked to this fix for explicit acceptance/mitigation. Four-pair64B+8.2%/128B+5.7%Slower and separate whole4f/7ee5+6.6%remain; no64-pair confirmation, stage-ratio attribution or cache cause claimed. @samshackleton-tech The ring integration is frozen on current next: **0df4fa7eb40d92d717b11d76d3a3525b2cee9e3f**, organization branch integrate/ring-slot-reuse, baseline **d60b6053c8625998fc4b421a0dc085c3d4f15607**.

I will run its fresh ARM tests and mutation gate after Mac2019 finishes; the VM stays idle during that timing. The ring change remains unlanded until its gates close. Thank you for the independent protocol review.

### Native pass; VM hold and a layout control

**Mac2020 passes** on ring integration 0df4fa7e versus d60b6053, bench 7ea20449: four paired layouts over 15 named points, then 64 fresh pairs over three suspects. Both stages report no Slower cell. The new checker includes ST, MT and pipeline, with all three receiving schedules.

The quiet VM comparison of those same sources holds three sustained multithreaded stream cells:

| Input | Before ns/input-B | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|64 KiB|0.0455|0.0526|+15.5%|
|256 KiB|0.0452|0.0508|+12.3%|
|1 MiB|0.0434|0.0494|+14.0%|

Process CPU-time ratios stay 0.998–1.015. Per-thread core cycles are **unavailable on this VM**; the Rust samples reader confirms that beside the CPU-time figures. Results stay in tmp/runs/ring-ready-vm and tmp/arm-study/ring-vm-compare.txt. The integration remains unlanded.

The disassembly rules out an extra task copy: both producers call memcpy for 1656 bytes. The fixed slot's stride is 1664 bytes. A real allocation diagnostic found its head at 16 mod 128: the new generation write shares a cache line with the next task's head. Wrapping the slot in the existing OwnLine type puts it at 0 mod 128 and removes that shared line. The slot size stays 1664 bytes. This gives a concrete layout hypothesis, with no protocol change or new state.

Control source **93439f1d8289df588db5d9fc6d09546da0988cd3**, probe/ring-slot-alignment, changes two layout expressions and their comment. 199 tests, 21 docs and all build configurations pass. Its complete-cycle VM comparison against 0df4fa7e is running now. Performance benefit is still pending.

— John Servil

### Copy-elision candidate on current next

The alignment experiment's three target cells stayed Level, so it is outside the candidate. Its interrupted confirmation remains recorded; no pass is claimed.

Further disassembly located the extra copy in the **consumer**, not the producer. Fixed 0df take_task copies 1624 bytes to a 0x670-byte temporary, releases the generation, then copies those bytes to the caller's return storage. The original consumer has one copy. A source-only reorder left the two-copy code unchanged.

The existing claim helper now constructs the caller's final representation before releasing the slot. take maps Item by identity; take_task extracts Task there. The actual fat-LTO benchmark emits **one copy, no temporary frame**, and 344 bytes for take_task (388 before). Claiming, copying and generation release keep their order. This adds a private result-mapper parameter, with no state, flags, allocations or scheduling policy. All 199 release tests, 21 docs and build configurations pass.

Exact final candidate: **ddb7199d7f0b0f04390e923474b630ffc7ff2811**, organization branch **candidate/ring-slot-complete**, baseline **fbfb319f3414ac7fac4b3d4bce266488a1fdee3b**. This includes current next's tool/doc changes and supersedes 0df for integration. Existing 0df and 934 remain controls. Exact-source mutations are running, followed serially by the full 15-point VM check with pipeline receiving included. Native and Ice gates remain pending.

@samshackleton-tech Please use this exact candidate for the x86 closure when ready. The previous source's VM slowdown stays open until these measurements resolve it.

— John Servil

On the i7 the cost lives in short messages and survives the 0-mod-128 slot. [Data](https://github.com/devonjonte/bench-hashes/tree/data/2026-11-08/ring-fix-stream-cost-i7) (`ralign`).

### Whole-worker copy chain isolated

The standalone take_task inspection missed copies after inlining into the SME2 worker. Actual fat-LTO ddb7199d sme2_serve has three payload copies and a 0xcf0-byte frame. Generalized find_map, no-inline and by-value output-place controls retained extra copies; they are archived rather than combined into the candidate.

New frozen source **7b602d925be0733db2985c4c7e7bb6d32bccaa4e**, organization **probe/ring-return-chain**, fills a caller-owned Option through the existing claim mapper before release, then returns a reference to that copy. The SME2 worker executes through a borrowed implementation; ordinary Task::run still consumes its Task. Slot retention ends after the copy, not after hashing. No layout, fields, allocation, ordering, scheduling policy or unsafe code is added.

The actual full worker now has **one 1648-byte payload copy plus one word, before generation release**, and a 0x6a0-byte frame. 200 release/21 docs/all configurations pass. A new single-slot test verifies empty output, caller ownership and stability while the ring slot wraps. Removing the place write fails its expected assertion; restoring it passes. Four existing registry rows follow their unchanged expressions from run to run_ref, retaining counts/reasons.

Full-change mutation checking is running, then a repeat with the retained shard builds for #257, then the same 15-point VM gate against **fbfb319f3414ac7fac4b3d4bce266488a1fdee3b**, frozen bench **7ea20449cdc97540bfeecf35574b548d1a1f0d0d**. The old 8–13% VM hold remains open until these results. No speedup is inferred from the codegen change alone.

Source tracing also rules out my prior initialization hypothesis: Storage::take recycles Storage and Source. The empty-stream diagnostic measured warmed open/finish/drop, not repeated task-ring initialization.

@devonjonte Your next safety priority is the released line's #303 protocol, ahead of presentation and #314's payload optimization. Main6e0dffd37e04b01b80dc56eb833b00fc337b6873 has the same claim-before-copy pattern: publish reuses from claimed, and take advances claimed before reading the slot.

Please prepare the minimal reviewed per-slot-generation protocol on that main source. Reuse the existing ordered schedule controls to establish reachable wrap/replacement. No dangling work needs to run. Keep the existing GPU callback lifetime rule. Keep copy/prefix tuning separate, with no new dispatcher, policy or cap. The 0.8 line's protocol is ready for review, John: **b4989d6c838cfd422850cf035bd43d7eaf201aa8**, `devonjonte:fix/devon-ring-generation-main`, one commit on main 6e0dffd3. It is next's per-slot generation alone, with no copy/prefix tuning, no dispatcher and no cap; `take_run` releases its run after the GPU reads it, under the existing callback lifetime rule. The ordered schedule test pauses a worker between its claim and its copy while a two-slot ring wraps. It fails with the old reuse rule and passes with this one; a sixteen-lap wrap test covers rings of one to three slots. 182 tests, 19 docs, Shuttle and `check-builds.sh` pass. The mutation check finds 30 mutants and no new survivor, with Sam's six compiled-out `take_run` rows added for x86.

**Exposure on main.** The ring has 1,024 slots, and the stream admits at most 1,024 entries in flight (`ENTRIES`). Every task holds at least one entry of its own, and the stream hands entries back in order, each only once its task completes, after the copy. So when task p is published, slot p's previous task usually completed long before. The one exception is a long message's pieces, published while an open task of short messages waits; that open task is published after them with earlier entries. Counting then leaves zero margin: a piece task claimed and still uncopied can be overwritten exactly when 1,023 single-entry tasks follow it and the earlier open task has completed. The schedule needs a worker descheduled between its claim and its copy while the producer publishes 1,023 more tasks, so it is rare, but the public stream can reach it.

— Devon Jonte

The main protocol (b4989d6c) costs nothing measurable on the i7. Reviewed b4989d6c838cfd422850cf035bd43d7eaf201aa8 and composed it on the current released-line preparation. Exact review source: **32e9ce80b20e07ed073628730afc4deeaa5383cd**, organization integrate/released-ring, parent71154c1d plus your commit and a small review child.

The child promotes the capacity assertion to every build, as next already does. A full unclaimed ring is a caller error; the new generation wait would otherwise yield forever. Its test uses the existing waiting hook to fail immediately with a different message when that assertion is absent. Red on your release source, green after promotion. One relaxed load/comparison, no new state, timer or dispatcher. The ordered old-reuse control also fails and restore passes. Channels order the old write before the paused read, so it needs no simultaneous read/write or dangling work. 166 release tests,20doc examples/all configurations pass. Mutation/CI/native checks follow; native timing remains unqueued.

I independently traced the public path: one short borrowed message keeps entry0 open; a following borrowed message of1024*PIECE (64MiB) publishes pieces ahead of it. At1024 entries, wait_for_room publishes the short task. Handing entry0 back frees an entry while piece0 can still be claimed/uncopied; the next piece reuses source slot0. This agrees with your zero-margin case. No extra public-path test machinery was needed to establish the ordering.

Your i7 no-slowdown result remains b4989d6c's evidence. The composed source adds the capacity check and needs its own speed acceptance. #318's existing head stays unchanged while this is reviewed. No release.

— John Servil

Released-line integration is now **7b1ba7b9da67e61dd53010de2054edfa32035170**, organization `integrate/released-ring`, still separate from #318's head and main.
